title: An outsider within: The paradox of the Europe-Turkey relationship – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Turkey is an 'embedded outsider': a middle power that builds strategic autonomy from inside NATO and the EU economic system, backed by a $10bn arms industry, expeditionary military, energy-corridor geography and mediation access — yet dependent on Europe for markets, capital and technology. The authors urge Europe to stop seeking Turkish alignment and instead practise 'managed interdependence': bring Turkey into European defence procurement, modernise the customs union and use targeted conditionality.

insights.claim: Turkey is neither drifting away from the West nor coming home: it builds strategic autonomy from inside Western structures because that is where its leverage lies.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Stop pricing binary 'Turkey pivots East/West' scenarios; expect persistent hedging.
insights.quote: Turkey is neither drifting away from the West nor it is coming home.
insights.locator: Turkey is neither drifting away from the West

insights.claim: A post-Erdogan government would be more democratic and predictable but would not abandon defence autonomy, regional activism or balancing among great powers, because those rest on elite consensus, a domestic defence industry, bases on three continents and geography.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: An opposition win would lower governance/institutional risk premia but not change Turkey's foreign-policy fundamentals.
insights.quote: A post-Erdogan Turkey would therefore be a different kind of embedded outsider, not a former one.
insights.locator: A post-Erdogan Turkey would therefore

insights.claim: Turkish public opinion favours neutrality: a March 2026 MetroPoll found 68.1% wanted Turkey neutral between Iran and the US (22.6% pro-Iran, 2.1% pro-US/Israel), and a 2022 Kadir Has survey found only 21.5% backed sanctioning Russia.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Domestic politics make Turkish participation in Russia or Iran sanctions unlikely under any government.
insights.locator: The Iran war reveals a similar picture

insights.claim: Turks' main fear about a collapsing Iran is refugee flows, renewed Kurdish insurgency, economic disruption and an emboldened Israel, not affection for Tehran.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Iran instability is a direct risk channel for Turkish assets (border, migration, trade).
insights.locator: The Iran war reveals a similar picture

insights.claim: In August 2026 Turkey joined Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, a trilateral pact with Article 5-like guarantees dubbed a 'Muslim NATO', though it lacks integrated command, joint planning and shared threat perception.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Signals Turkish-Gulf defence alignment and potential Saudi demand for Turkish arms; so far more political than operational.
insights.locator: In August 2026, Turkey joined Saudi Arabia

insights.claim: Erdogan's close relationship with Trump gives Turkey unusual leverage over Washington and an alternative route into the Western system, reducing the immediate cost of ignoring Brussels.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: US-Turkey personal diplomacy can deliver deals (e.g. arms sales) outside EU frameworks.
insights.locator: The return of Donald Trump somewhat complicates

insights.claim: The EU accounts for 42.7% of Turkey's goods exports and 35.3% of its imports, with trade volume of €217.6bn in 2025 plus €42.1bn in services trade in 2024.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Turkish exporters' earnings are tightly tied to the European cycle.
insights.locator: The numbers remain striking despite political tensions

insights.claim: Turkey received roughly $200bn of foreign-equity inflows in 2003-2025, about 60% from the EU, and the West as a whole supplies about 70% of Turkey's FDI; Chinese firms were outside the top 20 investment sources in 2024.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Turkish capital-account health depends on Western investor sentiment; China is not a substitute financier.
insights.locator: European capital has been equally important

insights.claim: Turkey has aligned 24,597 national standards with European ones, a 99.5% harmonisation rate with CEN/CENELEC, embedding Turkish factories in European automotive, appliance, machinery, textile and electronics supply chains.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Supports Turkey as a nearshoring hub for European manufacturers.
insights.locator: Trade volumes understate the depth of integration

insights.claim: BYD is building a $1bn plant in Turkey that will benefit from access to the EU market via the customs union.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Turkey is a potential backdoor for Chinese EVs into the EU — watch EU tariff/rules-of-origin responses.
insights.locator: Ankara has tried to diversify

insights.claim: The 1996 customs union is outdated, excluding services, digital trade, public procurement, agriculture and climate regulation; the Commission proposed modernisation in 2016 but the European Council has not approved a mandate.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: A modernisation mandate would be a material positive catalyst for Turkish services, agriculture and procurement-exposed sectors.
insights.locator: This dependence also comes with a political irritation

insights.claim: Chronic macro fragility — high inflation, a weak lira and dependence on external financing — sets a hard ceiling on Turkish autonomy; inflation peaked at 85.5% in October 2022 and remained above 32% in mid-2026.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Disinflation remains incomplete; lira and financing needs keep Ankara dependent on Gulf and Western capital.
insights.locator: Yet Turkey’s economic fragility sets a hard limit

insights.claim: A currency crisis at end-2020 left Ankara needing external Western and Gulf capital, and de-escalation with former rivals (Saudi Arabia to Greece) from 2021 was the price of access to it.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Turkish foreign-policy moderation tends to follow financing stress — a useful signal linking lira crises to geopolitical risk.
insights.locator: By the end of 2020, Ankara concluded

insights.claim: Turkish GDP rose from about $241bn in 2002 to $775bn in 2008 and FDI surged from about $900m (2002-04) to nearly $12bn a year (2005-08) after EU accession talks opened, with EU states providing about three-quarters of inflows.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Historical evidence that credible EU anchoring drives large Turkish capital inflows.
insights.locator: Closer ties with Europe accompanied an economic boom

insights.claim: Turkish defence and aerospace exports reached $10.05bn in 2025, up from $248m in 2002; SIPRI ranked Turkey the 11th-largest arms exporter for 2021-25 with MKE, ASELSAN, Turkish Aerospace, Baykar and Roketsan in its global top 100.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Turkish defence exporters are a structural growth story; ASELSAN is the listed proxy.
insights.locator: Defence and aerospace exports reached $10.05bn

insights.claim: Turkey claims domestic content of defence production rose from about 20% to about 80%, but it remains dependent on imported engines and propulsion: the KAAN fighter relies on imported engines and the Altay tank uses a South Korean power pack pending the domestic BATU engine.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Engine/export-licence dependence is the chokepoint — Western suppliers retain leverage and Turkish programmes carry schedule risk.
insights.locator: Greater autonomy, however, is not self-sufficiency

insights.claim: Turkish defence firms are embedding in European supply chains: in 2025 Baykar and Leonardo formed the 50-50 LBA Systems JV in Italy for unmanned systems, Baykar bought Piaggio Aerospace, and Turkish Aerospace agreed a €2.6bn Hürjet trainer deal with Spain with substantial Spanish production.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Leonardo gains drone exposure via LBA Systems; Turkish co-production inside the EU is a route into European procurement.
insights.locator: One way Turkey has sought to overcome

insights.claim: Turkey's 2017 purchase of Russia's S-400 led to its removal from the F-35 programme in 2019 and US sanctions in 2020; the opposition favours resolving the S-400 dispute to reopen the F-35 path.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: An S-400 resolution (more likely post-Erdogan) would reopen F-35 and US arms business with Turkey.
insights.locator: Turkey’s purchase of Russia’s S-400

insights.claim: The EU's €150bn SAFE joint-procurement instrument is open in principle to candidate countries, but Turkey lacks the required bilateral agreement, with Greece and Cyprus viewing access through their own security disputes.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Turkish firms' access to SAFE money hinges on Greece/Cyprus de-escalation — a binary catalyst for Turkish defence exporters.
insights.locator: Yet that is roughly what has happened

insights.claim: The authors argue Turkey should be let into European defence programmes on a conditional, modular and reversible basis tied to de-escalation with Greece, progress on Cyprus, end-use guarantees, IP protection, sanctions compliance and third-country transfer limits.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Project-by-project member-state co-production deals with Turkish firms are the likelier near-term path than EU-level access.
insights.locator: Turkey should be let in.

insights.claim: Using its NATO veto on Sweden and Finland's accession, Ankara extracted commitments on the PKK and US approval of a major F-16 sale, showing it capitalises on NATO membership as much as it upholds the alliance.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Expect Turkey to monetise alliance vetoes for arms deals in future NATO decisions.
insights.quote: Turkey capitalises on its position in NATO as much as it upholds the alliance.
insights.locator: Yet embeddedness has not meant deference

insights.claim: Turkey monetises its geography as an energy transit hub despite producing little energy: Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan and the Southern Gas Corridor carry Azerbaijani oil and gas, Blue Stream and TurkStream carry Russian gas, Iranian gas enters from the east and expanding LNG terminals take US and Qatari cargoes.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Turkey is a key swing node for south-eastern European gas supply; regional disorder raises its value.
insights.locator: Azerbaijani oil and gas cross Anatolia

insights.claim: Turkey backs the $17bn Development Road linking Iraq's al-Faw Grand Port to Europe as an alternative to the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor that bypasses it, and Strait of Hormuz instability has boosted the project.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Hormuz risk strengthens overland corridor plays through Iraq and Turkey; IMEC faces a competing route.
insights.locator: Turkey has also invested in logistics

insights.claim: The Montreux Convention wartime provisions invoked by Turkey closed the Straits to belligerents' warships, mainly constraining Russia's Black Sea fleet while also limiting NATO naval access.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Turkey controls Black Sea naval access — central to any Black Sea shipping/security arrangement.
insights.locator: At the same time, Ankara refused to join

insights.claim: Turkey brokered the 2022 Black Sea grain deal with the UN, keeping a critical maritime trade route open for almost a year, while also being a key conduit for trade with Russia.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Turkey is the likely broker for any future Black Sea shipping or grain arrangement.
insights.locator: Since the start of the war in Ukraine

insights.claim: Turkey signed an August 2025 defence accord to train, equip and advise the army Syria's new government is rebuilding and has become its most important external backer, but cannot finance Syria's reconstruction alone.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Syrian reconstruction requires European and Gulf capital — Turkish contractors are positioned but funding-dependent.
insights.quote: Its ability to shepherd the transition depends, paradoxically, on the very Western relationships it has sought to loosen.
insights.locator: Syria is therefore where Turkey’s embedded-outsider

insights.claim: The Turkish-Israeli rivalry, sharpened since 2024 over Gaza and Syria, is structuring the region into rival camps: an Ankara-led Sunni grouping versus an Israel-Greece-Cyprus bloc; Israel has attacked sites earmarked for Turkish military installations in Syria.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: A structural Turkey-Israel rivalry raises eastern-Mediterranean energy and security risk.
insights.locator: Israel is another problem

insights.claim: The eastern Mediterranean is potentially the most dangerous Turkey-EU flashpoint: Turkey will not accept Greek territorial-waters extension from six to twelve nautical miles (declared a casus belli in 1995) and insists Cyprus cannot develop hydrocarbons without Turkish Cypriot agreement.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Offshore Cyprus gas development retains a persistent Turkish-veto risk absent a settlement.
insights.locator: As long as Cyprus remains divided

insights.claim: Targeted EU sanctions over drilling can raise the price of Turkish actions but are unlikely to change Ankara's position on core national interests; since Merkel left office no European leader has had comparable standing with Erdogan.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Don't expect sanctions to resolve east-Med disputes; a UN-led resource-sharing deal is the realistic upside scenario.
insights.locator: Tensions peaked in 2020

insights.claim: Turkey's mediation advantage comes from access rather than neutrality; it used its relationship with Hamas to secure the Gaza ceasefire deal including a disarmament clause, though Israel then vetoed a bigger Turkish peacekeeping role.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Turkey is a necessary intermediary in Middle East and Ukraine negotiations, raising its bargaining value with the West.
insights.quote: Turkey’s comparative advantage in mediation therefore does not come from neutrality but access.
insights.locator: Turkey’s comparative advantage in mediation

insights.claim: Turkish TV dramas were exported to over 150 countries in 2024, earning over $500m a year and reaching nearly a billion viewers; per-episode export subsidies were introduced in 2026.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Turkish content exports are a growing services export line with state support.
insights.locator: Perhaps Turkey’s most effective soft power

insights.claim: Europe should pursue 'managed interdependence' with Turkey: deepen cooperation where interests converge, tie benefits to reciprocal obligations and withhold access when Ankara acts against fundamental European interests.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Points to a sequence of self-contained EU-Turkey deals (defence, trade, migration, mobility) rather than a grand bargain.
insights.quote: The aim is not obedience. It is to make Turkey’s autonomy pay for Europe more often than it costs.
insights.locator: The more useful question for Europe

insights.claim: Modernising the EU-Turkey customs union in stages, with sector access tied to compliance and stronger dispute settlement, should be the centrepiece of the relationship and would strengthen the EU's industrial hand against China and America.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Customs-union upgrade would deepen nearshoring into Turkey for European manufacturers.
insights.locator: Modernisation of the customs union should be

insights.claim: As Europe takes on more of its own defence and Washington becomes less predictable, Turkey's military capacity, geography and defence industry become more valuable to Europeans, creating mutual rather than one-sided leverage.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: European rearmament raises the strategic and commercial value of Turkish defence suppliers.
insights.locator: The return of Donald Trump somewhat complicates

insights.claim: EU accession talks have effectively collapsed (16 of 35 chapters opened, one closed, frozen since 2018), and the authors argue candidate status should be left legally intact but politically dormant, avoiding the 'privileged partnership' label that is toxic in Turkey.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: No accession catalyst for Turkish assets; the relevant catalysts are sectoral deals.
insights.locator: Turkey’s political relationship with Europe

insights.claim: Turkish public support for EU membership remains substantial: 58% would back it in a referendum (spring 2025 EU delegation survey) and Pew found 56% support in 2024, rising to 66% among under-35s.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Latent pro-European sentiment underpins the upside case for a post-Erdogan re-anchoring.
insights.locator: Turkey’s political estrangement from the EU

insights.claim: The 2016 EU-Turkey migration deal reduced the relationship to cash for border control; the authors call for a durable framework with shared responsibilities, EU funding for Turkish municipalities, more resettlement and easier visas for Turks.
insights.speaker: Aslı Aydıntaşbaş, Evren Balta
insights.so_what: Migration remains a Turkish lever over Europe; a new framework would reduce weaponisation risk.
insights.locator: The 2016 migration deal reduced
